It's intrinsic in everything that you do. And 0:04:25.560 --> 0:04:27.960 I always love the perspective because I think that you 0:04:27.980 --> 0:04:30.240 guys see the game differently. And I really appreciate that perspective. And 0:04:40.230 --> 0:04:42.650 as a player, obviously, you were super successful. You played 0:04:42.670 --> 0:04:46.680 in the league. when did you start realizing, okay, now 0:04:46.710 --> 0:04:49.820 this is wrapping a little bit and I'm going to 0:04:49.860 --> 0:04:51.780 maybe try coaching at this point? 0:04:52.300 --> 0:04:54.720 Yeah, it didn't really, it didn't work out like that. 0:04:54.779 --> 0:04:56.800 It was, um, it was so funny when I was, 0:04:56.820 --> 0:05:00.580 I was late, I was finishing up in Kansas city and, um, 0:05:00.900 --> 0:05:05.070 their head of player personnel, um, player development actually said 0:05:05.089 --> 0:05:06.590 to me, you should get into coaching. 0:05:06.670 --> 0:05:09.470 So I did my defensive coordinator at the time. And, um, 0:05:10.380 --> 0:05:11.680 I kind of was like, I don't want to do that. 0:05:12.300 --> 0:05:15.040 I wanted to go back to London and just kind 0:05:15.100 --> 0:05:17.380 of work out what I was going to do next. 0:05:17.980 --> 0:05:21.680 And when you finish playing football, I'm talking to other guys, 0:05:21.700 --> 0:05:23.700 you kind of go through this, is if you haven't 0:05:23.760 --> 0:05:27.760 got the next thing you can definitely deliver your purpose into. 0:05:28.700 --> 0:05:30.229 As you go through it, you're kind of in that 0:05:30.290 --> 0:05:33.790 search mode. And my coach, Tony Allen, at the time 0:05:33.830 --> 0:05:37.430 from London, he was the head coach of the London Warriors, 0:05:38.020 --> 0:05:40.080 He just said, come down and help the guys out 0:05:40.180 --> 0:05:43.539 and share experiences and you can carry on training. 0:05:43.900 --> 0:05:46.150 They had a weight room down there and stuff. So 0:05:46.510 --> 0:05:46.790 I did. 0:05:46.870 --> 0:05:49.770 And that's when I kind of fell in love with coaching. 0:05:49.830 --> 0:05:53.909 I didn't know that that was something I wanted to do. 0:05:54.230 --> 0:05:57.620 And as it went through it, I kind of, I 0:05:57.630 --> 0:06:00.400 was actually, I fell in love with it probably as 0:06:00.480 --> 0:06:01.520 much as I did playing. 0:06:01.580 --> 0:06:03.360 And I realized I was way more prepared for it 0:06:03.400 --> 0:06:04.299 than I was as a player. 0:06:05.160 --> 0:06:05.820 What do you mean by that? 0:06:07.610 --> 0:06:09.610 Because as a player you're like when you're coming from 0:06:09.650 --> 0:06:12.470 another country at that time when I came. 0:06:13.270 --> 0:06:17.510 You're getting moved up at a rate that is not. 0:06:18.990 --> 0:06:22.340 At the same level as your development because it's like 0:06:22.400 --> 0:06:25.360 it's happening like oh you go to an NFL Europe 0:06:25.400 --> 0:06:28.760 workout you do well they throw you straight out there 0:06:28.980 --> 0:06:32.000 and you haven't played a high level of football you've 0:06:32.060 --> 0:06:34.920 never been had an install of a playbook to you 0:06:35.300 --> 0:06:38.560 and then I went to NFL Europe and then it 0:06:38.820 --> 0:06:42.880 was kind of a watered-down version of the NFL. So 0:06:52.620 --> 0:06:55.860 it was like that– it was less so I could 0:06:55.900 --> 0:06:59.020 learn it quicker. So I got chances to play, and 0:06:59.050 --> 0:07:01.210 then I did well there, so I ended up playing there. 0:07:01.230 --> 0:07:03.630 And then once you start getting comfortable, they just move 0:07:03.650 --> 0:07:05.089 you and they give you a shot in the NFL, 0:07:05.110 --> 0:07:07.580 and then it was like that was– that was a 0:07:07.660 --> 0:07:11.370 world apart the game was completely different um he was 0:07:11.390 --> 0:07:13.530 around people that were playing in one team for more 0:07:13.570 --> 0:07:16.590 than a year so they knew the system they could 0:07:16.790 --> 0:07:19.290 play in their subconscious they could make plays and they 0:07:19.330 --> 0:07:22.130 were confident they were grown men you know like and 0:07:22.360 --> 0:07:24.300 it was like so he was always uncomfortable and at 0:07:24.340 --> 0:07:27.780 times i think looking back i was probably like had 0:07:27.820 --> 0:07:31.300 a lot of imposter syndrome feeling like you're trying to 0:07:31.340 --> 0:07:34.530 find yourself but there's like there's football and there's all 0:07:34.550 --> 0:07:35.630 these cultural differences. 0:07:35.650 --> 0:07:36.890 And there was a lot of stuff going on in 0:07:36.930 --> 0:07:37.810 my life at that time. 0:07:37.850 --> 0:07:42.070 And then I got into coaching and I didn't realize 0:07:42.130 --> 0:07:44.880 I'd probably been coaching myself more than anyone had been 0:07:44.920 --> 0:07:46.160 coaching me the whole time. 0:07:47.200 --> 0:07:48.980 And I just found it easy. 0:07:49.320 --> 0:07:51.960 And I kind of, I knew I can see when 0:07:52.060 --> 0:07:55.900 someone doesn't understand something or I can see movement details 0:07:55.920 --> 0:07:59.660 that I looked at in other people to teach myself. And, 0:08:00.230 --> 0:08:03.110 can help people and that's where it started like fundamental 0:08:03.150 --> 0:08:06.380 development in england then like then it's more of that 0:08:06.420 --> 0:08:08.340 when you're coaching in england it's more putting people in 0:08:08.380 --> 0:08:10.800 the right place allowing them to have fun allowing them 0:08:10.840 --> 0:08:13.280 to play fast and then teaching the physicality of game 0:08:13.380 --> 0:08:15.900 how you want to play but then kick it forwards 0:08:15.940 --> 0:08:18.380 it kind of works at this level too. 0:08:19.110 --> 0:08:20.610 Yeah i was going to ask you about that because 0:08:20.650 --> 0:08:23.510 i would imagine learning the way that you did And 0:08:23.970 --> 0:08:27.310 you said it, you can recognize knowledge gaps in other people. 0:08:28.370 --> 0:08:31.240 You do that non-verbally as a coach as well as verbally. 0:08:31.560 --> 0:08:36.340 And so what about that process maybe builds connectivity with players? 0:08:36.960 --> 0:08:40.560 When you're seeing something that you can help somebody with 0:08:41.090 --> 0:08:43.610 in a player at any level, whether you were coaching 0:08:43.850 --> 0:08:48.079 London Warriors, Dallas, Atlanta, now in Seattle... Reaching into a 0:08:48.140 --> 0:08:50.660 player like that, what is that process for you? And 0:08:50.980 --> 0:08:53.280 I would imagine that was a little bit of a 0:08:53.300 --> 0:08:55.040 light bulb moment for you back then, is seeing that 0:08:55.059 --> 0:08:55.760 you could do that. 0:08:57.000 --> 0:08:59.400 Yeah, that's a great question. 0:08:59.500 --> 0:09:04.850 I think as you go through it, it's more you, 0:09:05.510 --> 0:09:07.950 like when you see those knowledge gaps in people, people 0:09:07.990 --> 0:09:10.610 want to fill the knowledge gap, but they also sometimes 0:09:10.690 --> 0:09:11.870 don't want you to know. 0:09:11.730 --> 0:09:14.590 That there is a knowledge gap, if that makes sense. 0:09:14.900 --> 0:09:21.850 Because you're dealing in a world where vulnerability is not 0:09:22.070 --> 0:09:24.350 always the right thing for them because you don't want 0:09:24.370 --> 0:09:26.010 to show that I don't know. This is a 0:09:32.000 --> 0:09:34.439 business and it's their job and the way they feed 0:09:34.460 --> 0:09:37.530 their families. So I think there's part of it that 0:09:37.590 --> 0:09:41.600 you have to connect and build trust and trust is 0:09:41.620 --> 0:09:44.200 built with consistency and being who you are and being 0:09:44.260 --> 0:09:48.290 authentic and then it's more about like feeding the group 0:09:48.330 --> 0:09:52.110 knowledge talking to people maybe asking certain people questions when 0:09:52.130 --> 0:09:54.290 you know the question is the answers for someone else 0:09:54.350 --> 0:09:57.910 and making them feel comfortable and connecting with all people. 0:09:57.630 --> 0:10:00.840 I think like it's not just like you and them it's. 0:10:01.160 --> 0:10:04.020 You and the collective and the collective allow you to 0:10:04.059 --> 0:10:06.660 connect with everyone you know like once that happens i 0:10:06.679 --> 0:10:10.300 think you've got you've got the group and that that 0:10:10.380 --> 0:10:14.300 those two-way those three-way conversations can happen and And then 0:10:14.350 --> 0:10:16.470 they feel good helping each other, you know, like that. 0:10:16.530 --> 0:10:19.770 That's when you talk about player-led leadership and all these things, 0:10:20.050 --> 0:10:23.069 these buzzwords that people say, that's the essence of it. 0:10:24.330 --> 0:10:27.050 Yeah, and you're getting a real crash course in this 0:10:27.110 --> 0:10:30.250 back in London too. And I think there's lots of guys 0:15:01.910 --> 0:15:02.710 in the league that do. 0:15:03.610 --> 0:15:05.450 I think you have to make it about them and 0:15:05.470 --> 0:15:08.370 the team and not about yourself and like how smart 0:15:08.410 --> 0:15:10.490 you think you can be because you can just overwhelm 0:15:10.530 --> 0:15:12.950 people and you can, you can go down a route 0:15:13.010 --> 0:15:15.990 of giving them too much and it freezes them at times. 0:15:16.030 --> 0:15:19.350 And you've always got to like find that balance and 0:15:20.030 --> 0:15:24.370 create that medium within your game planning, your development plan, 0:15:24.850 --> 0:15:29.140 your coaching structure of how is this with, with, the 0:15:29.180 --> 0:15:34.560 players in mind, can we execute? Well, Adam, thank you so much. And I know 0:15:49.250 --> 0:15:51.510 we're running up on time here, but I could try 0:15:51.550 --> 0:15:54.750 to pick your brain and relive the glory days from 0:15:54.770 --> 0:15:57.670 the UK, from the London Warriors forever. title: It looks like the Bears will get some key players back vs the Saints
channel_name: Take The North: A Chicago Bears Podcast
text: Dan Wiederer and Mark Grote discuss the likely return of runningback Kyle Monangai and corner Malik Muhammad against the Saints. Also, it looks like nickel corner Kyler Gordon will miss this game with a shoulder injury.

title: [FULL EPISODE] Bears look to avoid a letdown against Saints
channel_name: Take The North: A Chicago Bears Podcast
text: The Bears will be heavy favorites when they welcome in the Saints for their first game after the bye week. The goal will be avoiding a letdown. Dan Wiederer and Mark Grote unpack this matchup. The Bears have been wanting to get their run game back up to head coach Ben Johnson's standard, and the Saints might be the right team to do that against. And defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons still has defensive coordinator Dennis Allen gushing over the type of impact he has on games. Also, what do the Bears need to be wary of against the Saints?
